methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Terra Drone is a public-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, having completed its IPO on the Tokyo exchange. The valuation exercise confronts a constrained comp universe: while seven private peers operate within Drones & Autonomous—including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro—no public comparables exist in this sector. This structural absence of traded peer data materially limits valuation methodology.

The peer-median approach, which would typically triangulate valuation multiples across same-stage and adjacent-stage competitors, is not applicable here. The screening identified zero same-stage public peers, zero adjacent-stage public peers, and zero similarly-tiered companies meeting the minimum three-datapoint threshold required for statistical reliability. Expanding to all seven private-sector peers would violate disciplined comp selection, as stage heterogeneity and capital structures across this group (ranging from late-stage private to pre-revenue) would render any median multiple misleading rather than instructive.

Without sufficient public trading data or a sufficiently tight private peer cluster, traditional triangulation methods do not yield a defensible valuation range. The key uncertainty is Terra Drone's specific operational metrics—revenue scale, unit economics, and path to profitability—relative to the known private peer set. A credible valuation would require either: fundamental DCF work anchored to Terra Drone's prospectus disclosure, or serial transaction comparables from recent funding rounds within the Drones & Autonomous space. The current data set supports neither approach.
